summary: Dedicated tenant experiencing steady throughput loss due to background-batcher slot pinning and long-tail micro-batches
description:
Issue summary:
Holden Analytics is observing a steady decline in effective throughput for their dedicated pool over a 6-hour window. P50 latency remains acceptable but p99 and queue length spike intermittently. Customer reports that requests either queue for >3s or receive 503 during these periods. Impact affects several high-traffic endpoints using gptx-large-v1.

Impact:
- Customer production jobs (document extraction & chat) seeing ~30-50% drop in completed requests per minute for the pool.
- Increased tail latency (p99 > 4s) and intermittent 503/504s.
- Business impact: customer-facing SLAs degraded for automated workflows.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: holden-dedicated-us-east-1 (reserved GPUs, heterogeneous mix: A100+T4 fallback)
- Region: us-east-1
- Time window: 2026-03-10 02:20 - ongoing
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Send steady stream of medium-length streaming requests (~300-500 tokens) from multiple clients with concurrent streams (20-40).
2) Enable streaming + function-calling on gptx-large-v1.
3) Observe autoscaler behavior during sustained 15-30 minute elevated concurrency windows.
4) Monitor serving-runtime / scheduler metrics and slot allocation logs.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should scale predictably and scheduler should allocate slots without serialization. p99 should stay within SLOs.

Actual behavior:
- Autoscaler attempts to add capacity but allocation requests fail or are delayed. Serving nodes show small CPU/GPU utilization spikes and repeated batcher sidecar logs indicating "pinned_stream_id" retention. Scheduler reports slot fragmentation and repeated short-lived batch creation.
recent_metrics_and_logs:
Relevant excerpts from logs/metrics: 
- [2026-03-10T02:43:21Z] scheduler: allocate_gpu(pool=holden-dedicated) -> insufficient_free_slots (fragmentation=0.62)
- [2026-03-10T02:43:27Z] sidecar-batcher[gid=17]: pinned_stream_id=stream-3a9b locked_for=920ms
- [2026-03-10T02:44:10Z] runtime: kv-cache-growth tenant=holden key_count=1.4M mem_used=78%
- [2026-03-10T02:44:30Z] autoscaler: scale_request(+2gpus) -> pending allocation, offer_timeout=90s
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/holden-dedicated?orgId=1 (p99 spike series)
investigation_notes:
Initial triage by Support (Maya) and SRE (Ravi):
- Observed pattern: many short streaming sessions create micro-batches that pin a GPU slot while waiting for downstream function calls. These micro-batches do not pack efficiently into larger batches, causing slot fragmentation.
- KV cache for tenant increased substantially — likely due to many unique conversation keys and long contexts; this increases per-slot memory pressure and makes packability worse.
- Autoscaler issued scale requests but cloud/gpu allocator returned delayed offers because of global fragmentation and a concurrent maintenance window in the region.
- Sidecar-batcher version 1.9.2 has a known heuristic that retains stream affinity for 1s by default; under heavy micro-bursting this became >1s pinned due to downstream latencies.
- No kernel errors or OOMs observed on the GPUs, but slot serialization (short-lived exclusive locks) increased request queuing time.

Correlated evidence:
- Linked SUP-631210 showed similar small-stream fanout symptoms last quarter but had different root cause (eviction preemption).
- Heap and KV cache growth trace: https://logs.redwood.internal/queries?q=tenant:holden+kv_cache+grow
workaround:
Applied temporary mitigations at 2026-03-10T04:10Z: 
- Deployed temporary routing policy: route Holden's highest-throughput routes to a lower-concurrency model variant (gptx-mid-v2) for 30 minutes.
- Restarted sidecar-batcher on 2 affected nodes to clear pinned streams.
- Increased autoscaler aggressiveness flag (scale_cooldown reduced) and requested +2 spare GPUs from cloud (hot-add).
- Customer-side ask: reduce concurrency per client to <=15 concurrent streams until follow-ups are deployed.

Effect: these reduced p99 spikes by ~40% and dropped immediate 503s.
resolution_notes:
Temporary fix applied (routing + sidecar restarts + scale request). Root-cause hypothesis: interaction of long-tail micro-streaming, sidecar affinity heuristic, and KV-cache growth produced slot fragmentation preventing efficient packing; autoscaler allocation delayed by regional offer constraints.

Planned permanent actions (Engineering):
- Scheduler: implement "micro-batch coalescing" heuristic to defragment slot allocation (ENG-ASA-1720).
- Sidecar-batcher: reduce default affinity window and add adaptive release on downstream stalls (PR linked above).
- Autoscaler: surfaced allocation diagnostics to detect region-level offer starvation earlier and to auto-failover to compatible fallback pools.
- Customer follow-up: create a dedicated tenant-level KV cache caps advisory and add best-practice for streaming concurrency limits in onboarding docs.

Follow-up tickets: INT-46011 (scheduler coalescing work), INT-46012 (sidecar affinity tuning).
